title: Loss-tolerant line-provenance buffer for multi-format structured log ingress
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Problem: several services produce structured logs in different encodings (JSON, ndjson, compact-binary variants) and occasionally deliver records out of order or duplicated due to retries. Current pipeline has two failure modes we see in production: (1) transient spikes cause transient tail-latency and tokenized writes get dropped under backpressure, and (2) when reordering occurs, it is extremely hard to reconstruct line-level provenance for a tenant’s request when debugging latency spikes or errors.

Goal: implement a loss-tolerant ingress buffer that preserves line-level provenance, enables deterministic de-duplication across retries, supports schema negotiation for multi-format payloads, and offers a controlled memory/disk hybrid fallback so we meet latency SLOs while preventing silent data loss. The component should integrate with existing Kafka fronting and emit Loki/Elastic-friendly outputs downstream, and expose trace hooks and metrics for debugging and operational response.

Non-goals: full replacement of existing multi-format adapters (we continue to use the parsing adapters), heavy transformation of log payload contents; this ticket focuses on buffering, provenance, dedupe, and observable hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Buffer accepts JSON/NDJSON/binary-tagged payloads and forwards canonicalized structured events to downstream with preserved 'line_provenance' field
On 10% retry storms (simulated), downstream duplicate rate must be <=0.5% after dedupe logic
95th percentile end-to-end ingest latency (sidecar->downstream commit) remains under 800ms in steady state for typical tenant load profile
Dark-launch on 10 internal tenants for 2 weeks with metrics dashboards and no customer-visible regressions
Automated regression tests for out-of-order delivery and crash-restart recovery added to CI
decision_log: 2026-02-20: Storage engine trade-off - choose RocksDB for on-disk backing over LevelDB because of better compaction controls and predictable tail-latency on NVMe. Recorded as decision D-OBS-021.

2026-02-23: Dedup strategy - use (tenant_id, ingest_seq, line_hash) idempotent keys produced by sidecar to dedupe at commit time instead of best-effort TTL-based filtering. This favors correctness over minimal metadata overhead.
2026-02-27: Sequence window size - default 12s with per-tenant override. Rationale: balances reordering tolerance vs memory footprint; can be tightened for latency-sensitive tenants.
2026-03-03: Schema negotiation - adopt negotiators based on Content-Type header + protobuf/avro hint fields. Fallback: treat as JSON and attach original_encoding metadata.
2026-03-06: Loki label harmonization - expose 'tenant', 'service', 'env', and 'trace_anchor' labels. 'trace_anchor' maps to the canonical correlation id used for cross-system joins.
implementation_notes: Component name: ingest-line-buffer (Rust, Tokio). Runs as sidecar or as a shared agent in ingress pods.
API contract: accepts POSTs with Content-Type, tenant-id header, optional ingest-seq header. Returns 202 with assigned buffer_id and estimated flush timestamp.
Persistence: RocksDB per-tenant sharded column families. Small in-memory write cache + append log for fast ack. Periodic compaction and background flush to Kafka topic 'ingest-buffer-commits'.

Provenance model: add 'line_provenance' object to canonical event with fields: original_offset (string), original_encoding (string), sidecar_buffer_ts (ISO8601), buffer_seq (int). Stored as metadata, not indexed by default.

Dedupe: on commit, compute idempotent key = sha256(tenant_id + ingest_seq + line_hash) and store seen in RocksDB with TTL based on retention config. Consumer applies dedupe using this key before emitting downstream.

Backpressure & graceful degradation: when memory high-water mark reached, slow-path writes to disk and respond with 202 but set estimated_flush to 'degraded'. Metrics emit 'ingest_buffer_mode' gauge (hot|spill|reject). Reject only when disk is >90%.

Observability: counters for accepted, spilled_to_disk, deduped, forwarded, rejected. Histograms for buffer_enqueue_latency and commit_delay. Tracing: span created at ingress, tags: tenant, service, buffer_mode; span injection supports otel-baggage and x-trace-anchor.
Testing: add chaos tests that kill sidecar during active window and validate no lost commits for dark-launch tenants. Load test target: 50k rps spread across tenants with median event size 1.2KB.
